subject: TerraHealth SIG: scoped retention mapping and deletion evidence
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@terrahealth.com>
To: hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai
Cc: security@terrahealth.com
Date: 2028-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: scoped log retention and deletion evidence

Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for the SIG spreadsheet earlier. Our audit team (cc'd) had a few follow-ups specific to session/telemetry logs and a small set of tenant-level carveouts we discussed during the demo:

- We have three tenant classes (prod, sandbox, research). For prod tenants we need 365-day session logs retained for regulatory review, but for sandbox/research we'd like 30-day retention.
- We need a practical way to validate deletions for sandbox tenants (proof-of-delete for SOC 2 sampling). Specifically: will Redwood be able to provide an export of deleted records (hash list + timestamp) for a given tenant and time range?
- For investigations we may request temporary retention holds on handful of tenant IDs — what's the turn-around and evidence you can provide for those holds and subsequent releases?

I've attached our updated SIG-questionnaire (tab: retention) and a short list of tenant IDs we expect to scope for the carveout. Can you confirm whether you need anything else (IDs, example API calls, a formal POA)?

We have an external auditor deadline the week of 2028-07-11, so any timeline guidance is appreciated.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Security Program Manager
TerraHealth

Attachments: SIG-questionnaire-2028-06.xlsx

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@terrahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: scoped log retention and deletion evidence

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers to start:

- Yes: Redwood supports per-tenant retention windows. We can map prod -> 365d, sandbox/research -> 30d and enforce at ingestion or via TTL on the tenant namespace.
- Proof-of-delete: we can produce a signed export that contains record hashes + deletion timestamps and the tenant identifier. That export can be delivered as an S3 URL or pushed to your inbound SFTP.
- Temporary holds: we offer an internal control that marks tenant data as "preserved" and prevents TTL-driven deletion. Turn-around depends on the hosting mode: Hosted API customers get administrative hold changes within 24 hours; Dedicated/Private customers can set holds via API immediately if they self-manage.

I'll let Priyom (copied) share the recommended output format our compliance team typically provides (manifest + signed hash bundle) and any gaps for SOC 2 sampling. Kimberly I've looped in because she oversees evidence delivery and will confirm SLA and packaging.

Would it help if we scoped a 30-minute hands-on workshop this week to align on the exact tenant IDs and export mechanics?

— Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Cc: hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-11T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: scoped log retention and deletion evidence

Hi Samantha — following up with the concrete packaging we can deliver and a few constraints so your audit team has what it needs. Below is the recommended mapping and the artifacts we produce for customer-specific retention exceptions.

1) Retention mappings (implementation options)
  - Option A (enforced at ingestion): routing rule assigns tenant to retention class; oldest data pruned automatically. Recommended when you want clear separation.
  - Option B (post-hoc TTL): data tagged and background job expires records per tenant. Simpler for customers who want to self-manage temporary holds.

2) Artifacts Redwood can provide per request/period:
  - Retention manifest (CSV): tenant_id, retention_class, policy_effective_from, policy_effective_to, updated_by, signature_id. (sample attached: sample-retention-manifest.csv)
  - Proof-of-delete bundle: gzipped list of SHA256 hashes (one per record) with deletion_ts and a signed manifest JSON that includes the job run id and operator. We publish the job_id and manifest to your S3 bucket and retain server-side logs for 90 days for audit traceability.
  - Export proof for SOC 2 sampling: we can produce both the hash lists and a redacted sample of the deleted records (PII removed) on request.

3) Temporary hold process
  - Submit hold request via support portal (include tenant ids and reason). For Hosted accounts: 24 hours to acknowledge, 48 hours to implement. For Dedicated/Private we can implement via API in <2 hours if your SRE has access. Release requests follow the same cadence and we provide a signed release manifest.

Constraints / notes
  - For customers in Private/VPC mode who manage their own storage, we will provide the manifest and signed job artifacts but will rely on your storage admin for delivery confirmation.
  - Very large deletes (multi-terabyte) may be staged; proof-of-delete will be generated per stage.

Next steps I recommend:
  - Confirm the exact tenant ids list and preferred delivery (S3 vs SFTP).
  - Accept the sample manifest format (attached) or send a template.
  - Schedule a 30–45m workshop (we'll walk through a mocked deletion and show the manifest + S3 link).

We attached the sample manifest and a short text file with temporary S3 URLs (sample-log-export-urls.txt) to illustrate the delivery pattern.

If helpful, we can also produce a short CAIQ mapping doc that explains which CAIQ controls the artifacts map to (CC6, CC7, etc.).

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Compliance Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample-retention-manifest.csv, sample-log-export-urls.txt

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@terrahealth.com>

Thanks Priyom — this is exactly the level of detail our auditor needs. A few quick confirmations: 

- Delivery: we prefer S3 URLs with pre-signed links to our audit S3 (so we can ingest into our evidence tool).
- Sampling: for SOC 2 we'll ask for 3 random sandbox tenant deletions and one prod sample (redacted) for July audit sampling.
- Holds: 24–48 hour acknowledgement SLA is fine for hosted; for a handful of tenants we will request dedicated holds (we can indicate those IDs in the worksheet).

Let's schedule the workshop for Thursday 2028-06-14 at 10:00am PT — Kimberly, can you send a calendar invite with the proposed agenda (manifest format, delivery example, hold/release flow)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll upload the tenant list (final) to the SIG-questionnaire and flag the ones that will need holds.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Security Program Manager
TerraHealth
